before_row: | **MSF-32** `robust-mean-estimation-under-heavy-tails` — Robust Means under Heavy Tails | MSF-18; MSF-30; `functional-analysis/hilbert-space-geometry-and-riesz-representation`; `functional-analysis/banach-valued-integration-and-the-radon-nikodym-property`; `functional-analysis/compact-self-adjoint-hilbert-schmidt-and-trace-class-operators` | `alg-geometric-median-of-block-means`: for $n$ Hilbert-valued observations and integer $1\le k\le n$, partition indices deterministically into $k$ blocks of sizes $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ or $\lceil n/k\rceil$, compute block means, and return the minimum-norm minimizer of the sum of distances to those means. Writing $V=\operatorname{span}\{m_1,\ldots,m_k\}$ for the block means, orthogonal projection $P_V$ gives $\|z-m_i\|^2=\|P_Vz-m_i\|^2+\|z-P_Vz\|^2$, so every minimizer lies in $V$. On finite-dimensional $V$, continuity and coercivity give a nonempty compact minimizer set, which is convex; the published `thm-projection-onto-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set` supplies its unique minimum-norm point under that item's Countable Choice hypothesis. `lem-measurable-minimum-norm-geometric-median-selection` is the local Borel design: fix a countable dense $D\subset H$; for each $\lambda>0$, $G_\lambda(m,z)=\sum_i\|z-m_i\|+\lambda\|z\|^2$ has a unique minimizer. Its infimum over $D$ is Borel in the input tuple $m$, and the first enumerated $q\in D$ within $1/r$ of that infimum is Borel and converges to the minimizer by the strong-convexity gap bound. For $\lambda=1/s\downarrow0$, the regularized minimizers lie in $V$ and have norm at most that of the minimum-norm minimizer of the original objective; every cluster point minimizes the original objective by the regularized objective inequality. Finite-dimensional compactness and uniqueness therefore give convergence to that minimum-norm point. This limit is Borel, so block averaging and the geometric-median algorithm are Borel on the separable Hilbert data space; no weak compactness or reflexivity is needed. `thm-finite-variance-geometric-median-mean-bound`: for iid Borel observations in a separable real Hilbert space, define $\mathbb E_B$ as Bochner expectation, $\mu=\mathbb E_B X$, and $\Sigma=\mathbb E_B[(X-\mu)\otimes(X-\mu)]\in S_1(H)$. A Borel map into separable $H$ is strongly measurable by finite-valued measurable approximants that choose the nearest among the first $m$ vectors of a fixed dense sequence. $E\|X\|^2<\infty$ gives Bochner integrability of $X$; the rank-one map is strongly measurable and $\|x\otimes y\|_1=\|x\|\|y\|$, so the covariance map is Bochner integrable in $S_1(H)$. The Bochner norm inequality, bounded-trace map and rank-one trace identity yield $E\|X-\mu\|^2=\operatorname{tr}\Sigma<\infty$; the Bochner criterion is choice-free, while the trace-class and trace supplier clauses retain Countable Choice. $0<\delta<1$, and $k=\lfloor\log(1/\delta)/\psi(7/18;0.1)\rfloor+1\le n/2$, where $\psi(a;p)=a\log(a/p)+(1-a)\log((1-a)/(1-p))$, then $P(\|\hat\mu-\mu\|\ge11\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)\log(1.4/\delta)/n})\le\delta$. Prove by block Chebyshev, the independent bad-block count and Minsker's geometric-median lemma. `alg-univariate-trimmed-mean`: split $2N$ clean iid observations into two groups of $N$, allow at most $2\eta N$ arbitrary replacements in total across both groups, use one half to set empirical quantiles at levels $\epsilon$ and $1-\epsilon$, and winsorize/average the other half; either half may receive all $2\eta N$ replacements. Set $\epsilon=8\eta+12\log(4/\delta)/N$ and require $X$ to have an absolutely continuous law and finite variance, $0<\delta<1$, $\delta\ge e^{-N/4}$, and $0<\epsilon\le1/4$. Use nearest-rank order statistics $r(p)=\lceil pN\rceil$; prove the two cutoffs are ordered and all quantile arguments in $E(4\epsilon,X)$ lie in $[0,1]$. For $E(\epsilon,X)=\max\{E[|X-Q_{\epsilon/2}(X)|1_{X\le Q_{\epsilon/2}(X)}],E[|X-Q_{1-\epsilon/2}(X)|1_{X\ge Q_{1-\epsilon/2}(X)}]\}$, `thm-univariate-trimmed-mean-under-replacement` gives $|\hat\mu-\mu|\le3E(4\epsilon,X)+2\sigma_X\sqrt{\log(4/\delta)/N}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$; the second tail clause is $|\hat\mu-\mu|\le10\sqrt\epsilon\sigma_X$ with probability at least $1-4e^{-\epsilon N/12}$. The source says atoms can be included by adjustment but does not supply that proof; retain an explicit tie-robust extension obligation rather than count it as source-proved. `alg-multivariate-trimmed-mean`: split $2N$ clean iid observations into first/second groups $(X_i,Y_i)$ and permit at most $2\eta N$ arbitrary replacements total across both groups, so either half may receive all of them. Set $\epsilon=\max(10\eta,2560\log(2/\delta)/N)$ and require $\epsilon\le1$. In every unit direction $v$, use second-half projections to form nearest-rank quantiles $\alpha_v,\beta_v$ at $\epsilon/2$ and $1-\epsilon/2$, and let $U_Q(v)$ be the first-half projected average winsorized at $[\alpha_v-Q,\beta_v+Q]$. Form $\Gamma(v,Q)=\{z:|\langle z,v\rangle-U_Q(v)|\le2\epsilon Q\}$ and $\Gamma(Q)=\bigcap_{v\in S^{d-1}}\Gamma(v,Q)$. For $j\in\mathbb Z$, set $K_j=\bigcap_{i\ge j}\Gamma(2^i)$ and $S=\{j:K_j\ne\varnothing\}$. If $S$ has a least element $j^*$, return the minimum-norm point of $K_{j^*}$; if $S=\mathbb Z$, return the minimum-norm point of $\bigcap_{i\in\mathbb Z}\Gamma(2^i)$; if $S=\varnothing$, return the first-half sample mean. Each nonempty $\Gamma(Q)$ and $K_j$ is compact and convex; the $S=\mathbb Z$ intersection is nonempty by nested compactness. For measurability, order statistics and winsorized centers are continuous in the data and direction; replace the sphere by a countable dense subset, express nonemptiness through the resulting countable closed constraints, and construct the unique minimum-norm selector by measurable projection/approximation. `thm-multivariate-trimmed-mean-under-replacement`: for iid $X\in\mathbb R^d$ with absolutely continuous law and finite covariance $\Sigma$, a known upper bound $0\le\eta\le1/10$ on the total replacement fraction, $0<\delta<1$, and $N\ge2560\log(2/\delta)$ (so $\epsilon\le1$), the repaired selector obeys $\|\hat\mu-\mu\|\le c[\sqrt{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma/N}+\sqrt{\lambda_{max}\Sigma\log(1/\delta)/N}+\sqrt{\lambda_{max}\Sigma\eta}]$ with probability at least $1-\delta$, by the source directional trimming/quantile and nesting argument. The source theorem advertises $\eta\in[0,1)$, but its displayed quantile construction is undefined when $\epsilon>1$; retain its rate here only on the explicit procedure domain. The interval $1/10<\eta<1/2$ requires a different estimator/proof; at $\eta\ge1/2$, two point-mass clean laws with zero covariance can produce the same half-and-half observed sample within the replacement budget, so no uniform covariance-only mean bound can hold. The source’s atom extension for the multivariate theorem also needs a separate tie-robust proof. Do not claim computational feasibility. B: heavy-tail mean, one corrupted block, and comparison of clean finite-variance and sample-replacement models. | F06 complete. Minsker, Lemma 2.1, Theorem 3.1/Corollary 4.1, PDF pp.3–8; Lugosi–Mendelson, Theorem 1 and proof, PDF pp.9–13, and Theorem 2/estimator/proof, pp.14–23; Minsker uniform bounds Theorem 3.1/Corollary 3.1, PDF pp.7–8, as a conditional alternative. The primary full text was rechecked at the multivariate estimator on printed pp.15–16, theorem on p.14 and proof §§4.1–4.2, pp.17–23. Preserve exact split counts, confidence ranges and replacement assumptions; citation does not supply totality/measurability or the local tie extension. |
